items.title: Priscilla Presley Still Faces Fraud Claims in Legal War With Former Business Advisers
items.summary:
A judge has rejected Priscilla Presley’s bid to dismiss fraud claims brought against her as part of a messy legal dispute with two former business partners.

Elvis Presley ’s ex-wife has been locked in a back-and-forth legal battle with her former advisers Brigitte Kruse and Kevin Fialko since 2023. Presley claims the duo committed elder abuse by stealing her money, while Kruse and Fialko allege they’re actually the ones who were wronged.

Related 

Priscilla Presley Sues Ex-Advisors for Elder Abuse, Alleging ‘Abhorrent Scheme’ to Steal Her Money

Kruse and Fialko’s fraud claims are premised on the notion that while they were working tirelessly to monetize Presley’s name, image and likeness rights — including for a skincare line and in connection with the 2023 Sofia Coppola biopic Priscilla — she concealed that those rights had actually been sold years earlier to Authentic Brands Group. Presley’s lawyers sought to throw out those claims as legally deficient, but Judge Mark H. Epstein ruled on Monday (Nov. 16) that they pass muster, for now.

“The court believes the causes of action are sufficiently pled,” wrote the judge in his decision, obtained by Billboard .

items.title: What Did 1998 Actually Sound Like? A Look Back at the Year That Changed Pop Music
items.summary:
There is something fascinating about the way younger generations listen to the past. Across streaming platforms and social media, listeners raised on unlimited access to music are digging into decades they never lived through, rediscovering forgotten singles, reviving old albums and dusting off records that once defined an era. Songs that dominated radio before they were born are finding new audiences, detached from the moments that produced them but still carrying traces of the world they came from. 

This renewed interest offers an opportunity to look beyond nostalgia and ask a more interesting question: What did the world sound like when these records were new? What were listeners hearing, what was the industry selling, and what cultural shifts were taking place beneath the surface of the charts? 

1998 is a particularly revealing year to revisit. Not because the charts tell us everything about a culture, but because, sometimes, they tell us what a culture is becoming before it has found the language to express itself. 

The Billboard Hot 100 throughout 1998 was a map of an industry in transition. Lauryn Hill, Brandy, Monica, Madonna, Céline Dion, Aerosmith, the Backstreet Boys and Shania Twain represented different sounds, audiences and ideas of what popular music could be, all competing for the same space. America was not listening to one thing, it was negotiating between several versions of itself, and somewhere in that negotiation, the center was shifting. 

Lauryn Hill’s The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill, released in August, became one of the year’s defining artistic…
items.t: What Did 1998 Actually Sound Like? A Look Back at the Year That Changed Pop Music

items.title: Leon Bridges Lands Fourth Adult Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘Talk It Over’
items.summary:
Leon Bridges scores his fourth leader on Billboard ’s Adult Alternative Airplay chart as “Talk It Over” rises 2-1 on the Nov. 21-dated ranking.

The track rises to the summit with a 10% increase in plays at the format during the Nov. 6-12 tracking week, according to Luminate.

“Talk It Over” is Bridges’ first leader since “Peaceful Place” in October 2024. Before that, he led with “Bad Bad News” in 2018 and “Smooth Sailin’ ” in 2016.

When “Talk It Over” debuted in September, it became Bridges’ 19th career entry at the format. That’s the fifth-most among soloists in the chart’s 30-year history, behind only Jack Johnson (27), Sheryl Crow, John Mayer (26 each) and Beck (21). Among all acts, Dave Matthews Band (including his solo entries) and U2 share the record, with 36 each.

Bridges released “Talk It Over” in August on the second of three four-song EPs that previewed his fifth studio album, Happiness Anytime . The full 12-track set arrived Sept. 25 via LisaSawyer63/Columbia Records. Produced by J Lloyd-Watson and Lydia Kitto of the British group Jungle, it reached No. 12 on the Top R&B Albums chart and No. 74 on the Billboard 200.

“Talk It Over” is also the first Adult Alternative Airplay No. 1 for Columbia Records since Hozier’s “Nobody’s Soldier” in November 2024. While the label boasts 14 No. 1s at the format this decade, it leads the list and Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart simultaneously for the first time in two decades, as Dominic Fike’s “Babydoll” (released via Sandy Boys/Columbia/Legacy) jumps 3-1 on the latter. Columbia last ruled the charts together in…
items.t: Leon Bridges Lands Fourth Adult Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘Talk It Over’

items.title: Individuals With the Most Grammy Nominations: Full List
items.summary:
When the nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards were announced on Monday (Nov. 16), Beyoncé became the first individual to amass 100 Grammy nominations. That milestone prompted us to take a fresh look at the most-nominated individuals in Grammy history.

Beyoncé received her first two Grammy nominations at the 2000 ceremony for Destiny’s Child’s hit “Bills, Bills, Bills.” The smash, which was the group’s first No. 1 hit on the Billboard Hot 100, was nominated for best rhythm & blues song and best R&B performance by a duo or group with vocal. In 2023, Bey surpassed the late classical conductor Georg Solti to become the individual with the most Grammy wins in history. (Solti landed his final two Grammy nods in 1999, the year before Bey received her first. He was honored posthumously for his album Georg Solti – The Last Recording .)

Related 

Beyoncé Makes History As First Artist With 100 Grammy Nominations 

Not all of these individuals did as well translating nominations into wins. Drake has received 57 nominations but has won just five Grammys – all in rap categories. He’s the only artist on this list of most-nominated individuals who has won fewer than 10 Grammys.

Here are the 18 individuals with the most Grammy nominations. We show their total number of Grammy nods to date; the span of years from the first Grammy ceremony where they were nominated to the most recent; and their total number of wins to date. I also identify any wins in the closely-watched “General Field” categories – album, record and song of the year; best new artist; and producer and songwriter…

items.title: Led By Ella Langley, Women Artists Shine in Grammys Country Categories
items.summary:
Ella Langley ’s starry 2026 just keeps getting brighter.

When the final nominees were revealed for the 2027 Grammy Awards, Langley was among the artists leading the way, with seven total nominations, including nominations in each of the Grammys’ Big Four categories: album of the year (for Dandelion ), record of the year and song of the year (“Choosin’ Texas”).

In doing so, Langley joined just 16 other artists ever to earn nominations in each of the Big Four categories in a single year, including country artist Bobbie Gentry, who was the first artist to achieve the feat, in 1968. That year, Gentry won the best new artist category, while her album Ode to Billie Joe was nominated for album of the year, and its title track was nominated for song and record of the year. Kacey Musgraves and Beyoncé were the most recent artists to have country projects take home a Grammy for album of the year, with Golden Hour in 2019 and Cowboy Carter in 2025, respectively.

The success of “Choosin’ Texas” stretches beyond Langley, as “Choosin’ Texas” and Dandelion garnered nominations for many of the song’s collaborators. Beyond nods in both Big 4 and country categories, “Choosin’ Texas” co-writer Joybeth Taylor also picks up her first nomination in the songwriter of the year, non-classical, while Miranda Lambert earns her first producer of the year, non-classical nomination.

Langley, Taylor and Lambert are among many women spanning musical genres who dominated this year’s Grammy nominations, including women earning seven of eight nominations for album of the year.

items.t: Led By Ella Langley, Women Artists Shine in Grammys Country Categories

items.title: How Many Times Has Ye Been Sued Over Samples? Here’s Every Single Lawsuit He’s Faced.
items.summary:
Ye (formerly Kanye West ) has been sued many, many times for allegedly sampling copyrighted music without permission. Here’s a breakdown of every lawsuit he’s faced, what songs it involved, and how each case ended.

Over the course of his prolific career, federal court records show the rapper has been sued at least 20 times over claims of illegal sampling (the use of a copyrighted sound recording) or interpolating (the use of a copyrighted composition) in songs, including a whopping 15 such cases since 2019 alone.

And that’s not counting cases where others have been sued over his songs, like a case filed in 2012 against Roc-A-Fella Records, or a recent case against UMG filed by members of prog rock band King Crimson, nor allegations that didn’t result in a lawsuit, like Ozzy Osbourne’s accusations in 2024.

Like most sampling lawsuits, very few of those cases against Ye have gone the distance, and the vast majority have ended in private settlements. But one of them went to trial in May 2026 , resulting in a rare opportunity to hear the artist testify on the witness stand about his approach to sampling — and why he’s been sued so many times.

“I pride myself on giving people what they deserve,” Ye told the jurors, referring to credit and royalties. “I feel like a lot of people try to take advantage of me.” A week later, a jury issued a verdict that Ye was liable for copyright infringement and must pay a six-figure damages total.

Over the years, what are the specific lawsuits Ye has faced? What songs were at the center of those cases? And how did each legal battle end? To…
items.t: How Many Times Has Ye Been Sued Over Samples? Here’s Every Single Lawsuit He’s Faced.

Rosalía has the second most nominations, shortlisted for the first time in nine categories thanks to her critically acclaimed album ‘ LUX ’, and close behind her with nods in seven categories include Ella Langley , Phoebe Bridgers , Miranda Lambert and Olivia Rodrigo.

Tracks up for Songs Of The Year include Rosalía’s ‘Berghain’ which she released with Björk and Yves Tumor , as well as Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘The Cure’, Ariana Grande ’s ‘Hate That I Made You Love Me’, Bruno Mars ’ ‘Risk It All’, Olivia Dean ’s ‘Man I Need’ and Taylor Swift ’s Toy Story 5 track ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’.

Last month, Rockstar Games confirmed that dance titans Justice had composed an original score for Grand Theft Auto 6 . So far, two songs from the project have been released –  ‘Flower In A Hurricane’, which features Tame Impala , SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard , and Gesaffelstein collab ‘Pusher’.

The fifty-track, three hour collection will be available to stream December 11 and the record will also be getting a physical release, with a range of vinyl available to pre-order now.

Before that, fans will be able to hear Justice’s music later this week (November 19) when Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases.

In a new interview with French publication Rockyrama , Justice’s Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay have spoken about their decision to work on the highly-anticipated video game.

“When [the offer] arrived on the table, we thought : “If there’s one video game we have to do, it’s this one.” As soon as we accepted and started working [on it], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game,” they said.

According to the band, Rockstar weren’t looking for a specific type of sound or music style for the Grand Theft Auto 6 score. “but rather the emotion that the music should give the player at specific moments.”

items.title: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?
items.summary:
In 1961, a group of Italian creatives crossed the border to collect anti-Franco resistance songs and share them with the world – sparking intense backlash from the dictator. A new documentary retraces that perilous journey

In the summer of 1961, four Italians crossed the Pyrenees into fascist Spain. Unknown to the border guards, their car was loaded with microfilm, a tape recorder and, tucked in the pocket of a writer and musician named Sergio Liberovici, a book of matches – each split in half, etched with the addresses of Spanish antifascists in miniature and glued back together, a hairline fracture concealing secrets that, if discovered, could result in jail or worse.

Along with Michele Luciano Straniero, Emilio Jona and Margherita Galante Garrone, Liberovici was a member of a leftwing collective named Cantacronache. Formed in 1958 and counting Italo Calvino and Umberto Eco among their collaborators, the collective was repulsed by the superficiality of Italian pop music and hoped to revitalise culture with Brechtian realism. At the time, Italy was fiercely divided into leftwing and rightwing political camps, and it was a record label, Italia Canta, linked to the Italian Communist party, that financed the trip. Its goal: to secretly document the resistance songs of the anti-Franco underground. It was a perilous task for all involved, but especially so for Cantacronache’s contacts.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?

The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.

items.t: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things

items.title: Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia
items.summary:
Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok

Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra, to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.

Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.
